title: No Cloud, One Answer
eyebrow: With clear weather the thirteen sky readouts stop being thirteen

actions.fyi: Diagnosis only so far. Nothing needs a decision from you; the next thing on this page is a cause, proved by switching it off.

content.label: Two different quantities, the same picture
content.lead: Weather set to clear. On the left, how much sky shows through the cloud. On the right, where cloud exists. Different questions, and not one pixel of the sky differs between them.

before.caption: How much shows through the cloud, clear weather

after.caption: Where cloud exists, clear weather — identical

blocks.label: It is all thirteen, in two groups
blocks.text: At clear weather the thirteen readouts collapse into exactly two pictures — seven land on one, six on the other — and inside each group they agree pixel for pixel, not approximately. Both groups are the plain sky. None of the thirteen is showing its own quantity.

content.label: Put weather back and they separate
content.lead: The same two readouts at six-tenths cover. They are different pictures again, so the collapse belongs to clear weather and nothing else.

before.caption: How much shows through the cloud, six-tenths cover

rows.title: It is the cleanest test the sky has
rows.note: No cloud means every cloud quantity must be zero. That is a fact about the world, not a number anyone chose, and it needs no reference picture to check. It is the first thing any sky measurement should be built on, and today it cannot be run.

rows.title: A broken readout would agree with itself
rows.note: While all thirteen return the plain sky, a check written against them goes green whether the sky is right or not. That is the habit we just spent a job removing from the readouts themselves.

rows.title: The sky's own notes already claim this works
rows.note: They say a readout is kept alive at clear weather on purpose. It is not, so the note is wrong as well as the code.

rows.title: At clear weather, every cloud quantity reads zero
No two of the thirteen agree, at any weather setting
The check goes red on today's build
rows.note: A check that only goes green proves nothing about itself.

decisions.title: This one goes before the other two faults
decisions.why: It removes the only sky test that needs no reference to judge against. The other two make individual readings wrong; this one makes the whole band say nothing.

decisions.title: The fix ships with a check that goes red on today's build
decisions.why: The fault hid for as long as it did because nothing looked at clear weather. A fix without a check is the same fault waiting.

next.if_nothing: I find the cause, prove it by switching it off, and fix it.

steps.step: Find and prove the cause of the collapse
Fix it, and add the clear-weather check
Then the control that still carries the cloud
